chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who left the state of Ihram until he entered the Haram (sanctuary), and he said: 'He returns to the miqat of the people of his land from which they enter Ihram, and he enters Ihram. And if he fears that the Hajj will be missed, let him enter Ihram from his place. If he is able to exit the Haram, let him exit.'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْمِيقَات: The designated stations for entering Ihram

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if they enter the Haram without being in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic principle of *rukhas* (dispensations) in Hajj rituals, balancing the obligation of proper Ihram with the practical necessity of not missing the pilgrimage. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*yusr*) when hardship (*haraj*) is anticipated, allowing the pilgrim to either return to the specific miqat of their region or assume Ihram on the spot if time is critical. This ruling underscores the flexibility inherent in Shia fiqh regarding the spatial requirements of ritual consecration.
